NKE.rationale: Nike's fundamental health and trajectory are severely impaired. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed revenue flat YoY at $11.28B but EPS collapsed 35% to $0.35, with net margin shrinking to 4.8% (from 9.4% a year prior). Operating income fell to $650M from $844M YoY, and operating cash flow plunged 76% to $430M. The company faces multiple structural headwinds: declining China sales (down 10%), margin compression from inventory overhang, EEOC investigation into DEI practices, 14,000 layoffs, and intensifying competition from On, Hoka, and New Balance. Management has guided for continued low single-digit revenue declines over the next three quarters and delayed gross margin expansion to Q2 2027. Valuation remains elevated at 27.7x PE despite deteriorating fundamentals, with the stock down 32% YTD but still trading above its 52-week low. Near-term catalysts are negative: Q4 FY2026 earnings (Jun 25) expected to show further EPS decline to $0.14, and the dividend payout ratio of 108.6% signals unsustainability. The combination of collapsing profitability, structural competitive threats, regulatory overhang, and rich valuation relative to deteriorating earnings power makes this extremely unattractive.
